bullets.text: Underwriting profit 12.7% in 2003 (target 4%), versus 5.8% for five years; ROE 29.1% (comprehensive ROE 35.0%); Agency auto was profitable in 45 of 48 states; all Direct auto states were profitable.
Companywide NPW +26% in 2003, surpassing the $10B milestone; PL NPW +26%; CL NPW +35%; Texas NPW grew over 30% following a six-month self-imposed restriction to protect claims handling quality.

Invested assets reached $12.5B; equity grew to $5.0B; debt-to-capital 23% (policy revised to <30%); repurchased 4.95M shares for $316.8M; premiums-to-surplus 2.6, with plans to slowly increase operating leverage in 2004.

Claims represent three-quarters of costs. Progressive hired and trained 3,300 claims representatives in 2003, improving handling on nearly 3.3 million claim features. Industry accident frequency fell unexpectedly, and accident severity remained well in check.

Ranked #3 in U.S. personal auto with 7.0% share (State Farm 20.1%, Allstate 11.4%); #1 writer in Agency (4.8%) and #3 Direct (2.2%); believes top 15–20 players will grow at smaller competitors' expense.

Policies in force grew 57% over three years. Customer retention propensity increased; the rate of increase flattened some from 2002 through first-half 2003. Estimating policy life and lifetime premium provides opportunities for improvement.

Completed over 200 rate and program revisions in 2003 to maintain rate adequacy. Cross-subsidization between states or products is never permitted. Progressive expects advantages from early positioning and rate adequacy to diminish to some degree.

Replacing its billing system within months to provide flexible bill payment options. Claims will deploy new workflow technology in 2004. Developing applications that allow Progressive and its agents to do more, easier and at less cost.

Opened 12 Claims Service Centers in 2003, reaching 19 total, providing end-to-end physical damage resolution. Centers provide benefits in efficiency, accuracy, reduced rework, and repair cycle times. Progressive seeks the appropriate balance between loss costs and LAE.

Competitors benefited from reduced frequency and improved pricing. Personal auto industry combined ratio is expected below 100% for only the second time in 25 years. Progressive expects its underwriting margins to move closer to 4% over time.
